question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$, determine whether $AB=BA$.
explanation:
Step 1: To test whether the two matrices commute, calculate both products because matrix multiplication is not generally commutative.
Step 2: Using row-by-column multiplication, $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 3: Reversing the order of multiplication gives $$BA=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 4: These products are not equal; for example, their $(1,1)$th elements are $2$ and $1$, respectively.
Step 5: Therefore, $AB\ne BA$. Thus, this pair of matrices illustrates the non-commutativity of matrix multiplication.

options.D: No, because both $AB$ and $BA$ are zero matrices
